findings.title: Node event callbacks corrupt the error exit code
findings.description: `packages/cli/src/index.ts:171-172` registers `handleError` directly as the `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` listener. Node invokes these listeners with a second metadata argument—an origin string for `uncaughtException` and the rejected promise for `unhandledRejection`. The new `exitCode` parameter therefore receives that metadata, and `process.exit(exitCode)` can throw `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` instead of terminating with the intended code. Register wrapper listeners such as `(err) => handleError(err)` or use event-specific handlers.

findings.title: Worktree resolution is discarded, allowing a false clean result
findings.description: Only `id` is retained from `resolveProjectWorktree`; the resolved `worktreeId` is discarded and `project.projectPath` is always used. When invoked from a registered worktree, the no-path mode scans the main worktree instead. More seriously, explicit paths are resolved relative to the worktree CWD but checked for containment against the main project’s document root, causing them to be silently skipped. The command can therefore report zero files checked and exit successfully without validating the worktree contents. Use the resolved worktree path, such as through `resolveOperationPath(project, worktreeId)`, and add worktree-specific tests.

findings.title: Commander-generated invocation errors do not use exit code 2
findings.description: Only errors reaching the `frontmatter` action are passed to `handleError(err, 2)`. Missing or unknown `validate` subcommands are handled by Commander before that action runs and use Commander’s default failure exit code, normally 1. This violates the documented 0/1/2 contract and makes invocation failures indistinguishable from validation findings for shell consumers. Configure the command tree to exit 2 for these errors and cover missing/unknown subcommands in tests.

findings.title: Missing projectPath is emitted as an unknown JSON error
findings.description: The missing-`projectPath` error is a known configuration failure, but the `UserError` is constructed without an error code. Consequently, JSON mode reports `"code":"UNKNOWN"` through `packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:48-54`, preventing machine consumers from distinguishing this condition from an unexpected failure. Use the existing `MISSING_CONFIG` error code.

findings.title: The wrong-docType test never exercises an invalid literal
findings.description: The test is titled “a wrong docType literal is still caught,” but every registered literal is expected to validate cleanly, and the unknown literal is also expected to pass. Because the validator selects the schema using `data.docType`, a registered schema’s singleton `docType.values` constraint cannot encounter a mismatched value through this API. The test therefore provides false confidence about the behavior it claims to cover. Either exercise a genuinely invalid value against an independently selected schema or rename/document the test to accurately describe the current lookup-based behavior.

structured_findings.summary: Node event callbacks corrupt the error exit code
Worktree resolution is discarded, allowing a false clean result
Commander-generated invocation errors do not use exit code 2
Missing projectPath is emitted as an unknown JSON error
The wrong-docType test never exercises an invalid literal
